scopeNoteAddendum: **v2.80.0 (Kings waves C-D — 1 Kgs 6, 8: the Temple and its dedication; 2 Kgs 4, 17: Elisha's miracles and the fall of Shomron):** five new entries: `ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus` (the Temple plan: 'porch', 'great hall', 'inner sanctuary', 'most holy place'; replaces the ASV 'temple'/'oracle' for the rooms), `shakhan-dwell-divine-presence-verb-cross-corpus` (1 Kgs 6:13; 8:12, canon-cited), `arafel-thick-darkness-divine-presence-cross-corpus` (Ex 20:18 MT; 1 Kgs 8:12, canon-cited; 'thick darkness', not 'cloud'), `beit-zevul-exalted-house-1-kgs-8-13-cross-corpus` (1 Kgs 8:13, canon-cited; 'an exalted house' after Ugaritic zbl), `he-anan-cloud-fills-the-sanctuary-cross-corpus` (1 Kgs 8:10-11, canon-cited; literal 'the cloud', reception confined to apparatus). `tzeva-ha-shamayim-...` now also governs the astral sense (2 Kgs 17:16 'all the host of the heavens'). appliesTo extensions for cherubim-ezek, kavod-yhwh, elohei-yisrael, karat-brit, ka-et-chayah, chei-x-oath, adonai-yhwh-divine-name, har-sinai-horev, ad-ha-yom-ha-zeh, olah, navi, davar-yhwh, elohim-imkha, hithallekh-lefanai, bethel-luz, rachamim (1 Kgs 8:50 'mercy'), chesed-solitary (8:23 'kindness'), matzevah, pesel, nichesh-laban, malakh-yhwh-messenger, seven-day-banquet, shamayim (1 Kgs 8 prayer 'heavens', 8:35 'skies') and eretz. Kings-specific decisions live in the 1-kings-woh and 2-kings-woh overlays v1.2.0.

entry.partOfSpeech: nouns (architectural terms of the Temple plan); qōḏeš haqqŏḏāšîm is a superlative construct
entry.literal: porch, front hall / great house, palace / back room / holiness of holinesses
entry.standardEnglish: porch / temple / oracle / most holy place (ASV, KJV); vestibule / nave / inner sanctuary / most holy place (NRSV); portico / Great Hall / Shrine / Holy of Holies (NJPS)
entry.wohChoice: In the three-room plan of the Temple: ʾûlām 'porch' (ASV); hêḵāl 'great hall' (NJPS, Alter; ASV 'temple'); dəḇîr 'inner sanctuary' (NRSV; ASV 'oracle'); qōḏeš haqqŏḏāšîm 'the most holy place' (ASV); habbayiṯ happənîmî 'the inner house' (literal). Where hêḵāl denotes a whole sanctuary or a palace (e.g. 1 Sam 1:9; 1 Kgs 21:1; Isa 6:1; Ps 11:4) it is rendered 'temple' or 'palace' by context.
entry.rationale: 1 Kings 6-7 describes the Temple as a 'house' (*bayiṯ*) of three successive rooms on one axis: the *ʾûlām* in front (6:3), the *hêḵāl*, forty cubits long (6:17), and the *dəḇîr* at the rear, a twenty-cubit cube also called *qōḏeš haqqŏḏāšîm* and 'the inner house' (6:16, 19-20, 27). The same plan recurs in 2 Chr 3-4 and in Ezekiel's temple (Ezek 40:48-41:4), and it has close Iron Age parallels in north Syria (ʿAin Dara, Tell Tayinat; Monson, *BAR* 26/3, 2000; King and Stager, *Life in Biblical Israel*, 2001). // (1) *hêḵāl* is a loanword from Sumerian é.gal 'great house' via Akkadian *ekallu*, meaning 'palace' or 'temple' in general; in the plan it is the main room (HALOT *hêḵāl* 3). The ASV 'temple' is accurate for the general sense but misleading in 1 Kgs 6, where the whole building is the 'house' and 'the temple of the house' (6:3) names one of its rooms; 'great hall' (NJPS; Alter) keeps both the function of the room and the etymology. (2) *dəḇîr* is the rear room (HALOT 'back room'; cf. Arabic *dubr* 'back'). The ASV/KJV 'oracle' comes through the Vulgate *oraculum* from the ancient derivation of the word from *dbr* 'speak' (Aquila and Symmachus *chrēmatistērion*), which the modern lexica reject; the line uses 'inner sanctuary' (NRSV). (3) *ʾûlām* 'porch' and *qōḏeš haqqŏḏāšîm* 'the most holy place' (superlative construct, GKC §133i) are kept from the ASV. // The decision is lexical and architectural and carries no interpretive content. The Raëlian canon's description of the Temple as a residence built to receive the creators (*The Book Which Tells the Truth*, ch. 3) is recorded only in labelled reception notes in the chapter commentary. // **Central housing.** The terms recur in Kings, Chronicles, Ezekiel and the Psalms (*dəḇîr* Ps 28:2; *hêḵāl* passim), so one decision should govern the corpus; the claim_type is *direct* because the room functions and the lexical senses are uncontested in current scholarship.

entry.partOfSpeech: verb, Qal (perfect with waw-consecutive, 1 Kgs 6:13; infinitive construct, 8:12)
entry.standardEnglish: dwell (ASV, KJV, NRSV); abide (NJPS at 1 Kgs 8:12)
entry.wohChoice: 'dwell': 'I will dwell in the midst of the children of Yisra'el' (1 Kgs 6:13); 'that he would dwell in the thick darkness' (1 Kgs 8:12). The related yāšaḇ 'sit, be enthroned, dwell' (1 Kgs 8:13, 27, 30, 39, 43, 49) is also rendered 'dwell' and is distinguished in commentary.
entry.rationale: *šāḵan* is the verb of settling or abiding, used of people and animals (Gen 9:27; Judg 5:17) and above all of YHWH's presence among Israel (Ex 25:8; 29:45-46; Num 5:3; 35:34; Deut 12:11 'to make his name dwell there'; Ezek 43:7, 9; Zech 2:14-15). Its derivatives are *miškān* 'dwelling, tabernacle' (central `brit-shalom-mishkan`) and the post-biblical *šəḵînâ*, the rabbinic term for the divine presence (BDB; HALOT; Cross, *Canaanite Myth and Hebrew Epic*, 1973, on the tent-dwelling sense; Mettinger, *The Dethronement of Sabaoth*, 1982, on name and glory theology). // In 1 Kings the verb occurs at two canon-cited sites: the conditional promise of 6:13, which repeats the language of Ex 25:8 and 29:45 ('I will dwell in the midst of'), and the temple poem of 8:12 ('YHWH has said that he would dwell in the thick darkness'). Every major version renders 'dwell', which is kept; the entry exists so that the two sites, and the related *yāšaḇ* 'sit, dwell, be enthroned' of 8:13 and of the prayer's 'your dwelling-place' (8:30, 39, 43, 49), can be audited together. // The Raëlian canon (*The Book Which Tells the Truth*, ch. 3) quotes both verses ('I will dwell among the children of Israel'; 'he would dwell in a cloud') in its account of the Temple as a residence of the creators. That reading is confined to labelled reception notes; the line renders the verb lexically. // **Central housing.** The verb is a cross-corpus divine-presence term (Torah, Kings, Ezekiel, Psalms). The claim_type is *direct*: the rendering is the consensus one.

entry.partOfSpeech: noun, masculine singular (with article at Ex 20:18 MT and 1 Kgs 8:12)
entry.standardEnglish: thick darkness (ASV, KJV, NRSV); thick cloud (NJPS at 1 Kgs 8:12)
entry.wohChoice: 'the thick darkness' (Ex 20:18 MT; 1 Kgs 8:12); 'thick darkness' in the poetic pair ʿānān waʿărāp̄el 'clouds and thick darkness' (Deut 4:11; Ps 97:2; Joel 2:2; Zeph 1:15)
entry.rationale: *ʿărāp̄el* is the dense, dark cloud of the theophany: Moshe 'drew near to the *ʿărāp̄el* where the Elohim was' at Sinai (Ex 20:18 MT = 20:21 ASV; Deut 4:11; 5:22), YHWH has *ʿărāp̄el* under his feet in the storm theophany (2 Sam 22:10 = Ps 18:10), 'clouds and *ʿărāp̄el* are round about him' (Ps 97:2), and the day of YHWH is a day of *ʿānān* and *ʿărāp̄el* (Joel 2:2; Zeph 1:15). It is distinct from the ordinary *ʿānān* 'cloud', with which it is paired (BDB; HALOT 'deep darkness, heavy cloud'; cf. Ugaritic *ʿrpt* 'clouds', as in *rkb ʿrpt*, central `rider-of-the-clouds-rkb-arpt-cross-corpus-ugaritic-hebrew-bible-storm-theophany`). // exodus-woh renders the Sinai site 'the thick darkness' (EXO-WOH-20:18, under the overlay `sinai-cloud-fire-thunder-trumpet-imagery-exodus-compositional-cluster-overlay`), and 1 Kgs 8:12 deliberately echoes Sinai in Shelomoh's temple poem; the ASV rendering is kept at both so that the echo stays visible. // The Raëlian canon's French quotes 1 Kgs 8:12 as 'il réside dans un nuage' ('in a cloud') and reads the cloud as a craft in orbit (*The Book Which Tells the Truth*, ch. 3). The Hebrew there is *ʿărāp̄el*, not *ʿānān*, and accuracy requires 'thick darkness'; the reading is confined to a labelled reception note. // **Central housing.** The noun recurs across the Torah, the Former Prophets, the Psalms and the Prophets. The claim_type is *direct*: the rendering is the ASV and consensus one.

entry.partOfSpeech: construct noun phrase (bayiṯ + zəḇul, genitive of quality)
entry.literal: a house of exaltation / of princely abode
entry.standardEnglish: a house of habitation (ASV); an house to dwell in (KJV); an exalted house (RSV, NRSV); a stately House (NJPS)
entry.wohChoice: 'an exalted house' (1 Kgs 8:13 = 2 Chr 6:2); zəḇul elsewhere 'lofty abode' by context (Isa 63:15; Hab 3:11; Ps 49:15)
entry.rationale: *zəḇul* occurs five times (1 Kgs 8:13 = 2 Chr 6:2; Isa 63:15; Hab 3:11; Ps 49:15). Older lexicography derived it from *zbl* 'dwell' (cf. Gen 30:20 *yizbəlēnî*), whence the KJV/ASV 'house of habitation'. The Ugaritic texts, where *zbl* is a title 'prince, exalted one' (*zbl bʿl ʾarṣ* 'the Prince, lord of the earth', of Baʿlu; *zbl ym* 'Prince Yammu'), have since established the sense 'elevation, princely or lofty abode' (HALOT; DCH; Cogan, *1 Kings*, AB 10, 2001; Mettinger, *The Dethronement of Sabaoth*, 1982). Isa 63:15 ('look down from the heavens and see, from your holy and glorious *zəḇul*') and Hab 3:11 (sun and moon stand still in their *zəḇul*) use it of a celestial height; in 1 Kgs 8:13 it presents the Temple as the deity's princely seat. // Modern versions render 'exalted house' (RSV, NRSV) or 'stately House' (NJPS); 'an exalted house' is adopted as a correction toward the lexical consensus, not as a lens choice. The same title is generally recognized in the divine name Baal-zebul, deformed in 2 Kgs 1:2-16 as Baʿal-Zevuv (Cogan and Tadmor, *II Kings*, AB 11, 1988). // The Raëlian canon quotes the verse from the KJV ('I have surely built thee an house to dwell in') as evidence that the Temple was a residence for the creators (*The Book Which Tells the Truth*, ch. 3). The line renders *zəḇul* by its lexical sense, and the reading is confined to a labelled reception note. // **Central housing.** The noun recurs in Kings, Chronicles, Isaiah, Habakkuk and the Psalms. The claim_type is *direct* (consensus of current lexica and versions).

entry.wohChoice: 'the cloud' (literal, with the Hebrew article) for the cloud that fills or covers a completed sanctuary: 1 Kgs 8:10, 11 (cf. Ex 40:34-38; Num 9:15-22; 2 Chr 5:13-14; Ezek 10:3-4)
entry.rationale: At the completion of a sanctuary the narratives report that 'the cloud' (*heʿānān*, with the article of the known cloud) covers or fills it and that the glory of YHWH fills it, so that the officiants cannot enter or minister: the tent of meeting (Ex 40:34-35), Shelomoh's Temple (1 Kgs 8:10-11 = 2 Chr 5:13-14), and, in the movement of the glory, Ezekiel's temple (Ezek 10:3-4; 43:4-5). The cloud is the visible veil of the presence (*kāḇôḏ*; central `kavod-yhwh`) and is continuous with the wilderness pillar of cloud (central `pillar-of-cloud-and-fire-ammud-ha-anan-ve-esh-divine-presence-marker-cross-corpus`) and the cloud of Sinai (Ex 19:9, 16; 24:15-18; central `sinai-theophany-ex-19-elohim-craft-descent-disavowals-volcanic-hypothesis-cross-corpus`) (Mettinger, *The Dethronement of Sabaoth*, 1982; Cogan, *1 Kings*, AB 10, 2001). It is distinct from *ʿărāp̄el* 'thick darkness' (central `arafel-thick-darkness-divine-presence-cross-corpus`), which 1 Kgs 8:12 uses in the poem that follows. // Every version renders 'the cloud', which is kept. // The Raëlian canon (*The Book Which Tells the Truth*, ch. 3) quotes 1 Kgs 8:10 ('The cloud filled the house of Yahweh') and reads the cloud as the creators' craft. This entry asserts only the lexical sense and the literary parallel with Ex 40; like the pillar-of-cloud entry, the line encodes neither a craft nor a natural phenomenon, and the reading is confined to labelled reception notes. // **Central housing.** The motif is cross-corpus (Exodus, Numbers, Kings, Chronicles, Ezekiel). The claim_type is *direct*.

changes.wohChoice: the host of the heavens ('host' as in the ASV, keeping the lexical link with ṣāḇāʾ in śar haṣṣāḇāʾ 'captain of the host'; šāmayim 'heavens' at this divine-realm site, under the register rule ratified at the Kings wave-A sign-off, 2026-11-01); the same rendering in the astral-worship sense ('and worshipped all the host of the heavens', 2 Kgs 17:16)
changes.rationale: *ṣāḇāʾ* is an army or organized company, and *ṣəḇāʾ haššāmayim* is the company of the sky. It has two senses in the Hebrew Bible. (1) **The heavenly retinue / divine council**: at 1 Kgs 22:19 (= 2 Chr 18:18) Mikhayehu sees YHWH enthroned 'and all the host of the heavens standing by him, on his right hand and on his left', and the host deliberates (vv 20-22); cf. Neh 9:6; Ps 103:21; 148:2, and the council scenes of Isa 6:1-8, Job 1:6-12 and Zech 3. (2) **The stars and celestial bodies**, especially as objects of worship forbidden to Israel (Deut 4:19; 17:3; 2 Kgs 17:16; 21:3, 5; 23:4-5; Jer 8:2; 19:13; Zeph 1:5), and as stars (Isa 34:4; Jer 33:22; Dan 8:10). The two senses are closely related in Northwest Semitic thought, where the gods of the council were associated with the stars (cf. Job 38:7) (E. T. Mullen, *The Divine Council in Canaanite and Early Hebrew Literature*, HSM 24, 1980; L. K. Handy, *Among the Host of Heaven*, 1994; M. S. Smith, *The Origins of Biblical Monotheism*, 2001). // **Rendering.** 'Host' (ASV) is kept because Kings uses the same noun for Israel's army (1 Kgs 1:19, 25; 2:5, 32, 35: 'captain of the host'), and the English should keep the lexical link the Hebrew makes between the earthly and the heavenly *ṣāḇāʾ*. *šāmayim* is rendered 'heavens' at 1 Kgs 22:19 following the recommendation of the Kings wave-A Reviewer (2026-11-01) that divine-realm uses of *šāmayim* take 'heaven(s)', as genesis-woh already does at its divine-realm sites (e.g. GEN-WOH-28:12), while weather and directional uses keep the central `shamayim` 'skies'. That recommendation was ratified at the wave-A human sign-off (2026-11-01), with 2 Kgs 2:1, 11 'to the heavens'; this verse, YHWH's council around his throne, is the clearest divine-realm site in Kings. The plural keeps the Hebrew form visible; the ASV singular 'host of heaven' is recorded in commentary. In the astral sense the same rendering is kept (2 Kgs 17:16 'all the host of the heavens', Kings wave D, v2.80.0), so that one Hebrew phrase has one English form across its two related senses; the commentary at each site states which sense is in play. // **Bidirectional cross-references.** This is the Hebrew-side entry called for by `divine-council-phr-mad-cross-corpus-ugaritic-akkadian-hebrew-bible` (Ugaritic *pḫr mʿd*), and it clusters with `bn-ilm-sons-of-god-cross-corpus-ugaritic-hebrew-bnei-elohim` (the council's membership). // **Reception, apparatus only.** The Raëlian canon (*The Book Which Tells the Truth*, ch. 3) quotes 1 Kgs 22:19 ('all the host of heaven standing by him') as the prophet's vision of the creators. That reading is recorded only in a labelled reception note in the chapter commentary; this entry asserts only the lexical sense and the scholarly council interpretation, and the line encodes neither a fleet nor personnel. // The claim_type is *direct*: the grammar and both senses of the phrase, and the council reading of 1 Kgs 22:19, are scholarly consensus.
